sources.title: GPT-5.5 Instant: smarter, clearer, and more personalized
sources.evidence: May 5, 2026 announcement releases the exact model in ChatGPT and explicitly maps it to the API alias chat-latest. It documents text responses, image understanding, web search and use of uploaded files. It does not identify gpt-5.5-instant as a standalone API endpoint or disclose parameter counts.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 Instant System Card
sources.evidence: The PDF cover is dated May 4, one day before public launch. It equates GPT-5.5 Instant with gpt-5.5-instant and distinguishes it from GPT-5.5 Thinking. Section 8 states the model is deployed at low reasoning effort and evaluated at xhigh. Training and exact-model evaluation tables contain no total/active parameter count or block architecture.

sources.title: Chat Latest API model documentation
sources.evidence: Current mutable alias documentation lists 400,000 context, 272,000 maximum input, 128,000 maximum output, text/image input, text output, Chat Completions, Responses and function calling. It identifies only the latest Instant model and says its underlying snapshot changes regularly; it does not bind these current limits to GPT-5.5 Instant. It has a cached-input price but no explicit prompt_caching feature.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: May 5 launches chat-latest. May 28 and June 24 update that alias; August 6 and October 7 also update it. The later alias entries do not name GPT-5.5 Instant, so current alias specifications cannot establish the original model capacity.

sources.title: Foundry Models sold by Azure: GPT-chat-latest
sources.evidence: The primary provider table lists May 5, May 28 and June 24 versions of gpt-chat-latest at 128,000 context with 111,616 input and 16,384 output; August 6 is 400,000, October 7 is 128,000. These are provider/version limits. It states fixed nonzero reasoning, Chat Completions/Responses and function/tool calling. The page maps the provider name to OpenAI chat-latest; it does not establish an OpenAI-hosted GPT-5.5 Instant context limit.

sources.title: How we built a realtime system for responsive voice AI in six months
sources.evidence: The later engineering article gives an explicit GPT-5.5 Instant delegation example. In the same delegation section it describes persistent frontier-model inference sessions, prefilling and prompt caching, plus reasoning/tool round trips. This is an operational binding for a qualified broad caching inference. The separate voice-model KV compaction section is not transferred to Instant.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: The guide explicitly applies to models before GPT-5.6 and explains OpenAI prompt caching through Transformer attention key/value projections. Combined with the example-bound Instant delegation caching explanation, it supports only a qualified broad Transformer-based classification, not a full block inventory, dense/MoE layout or numerical size.

sources.title: Improving health intelligence in ChatGPT
sources.evidence: June 18, 2026 article explicitly compares GPT-5.5 Instant with other models through health evaluations and physician-rated responses. It discusses model improvements and evaluation/training input, but its exact-model results are performance measures, not parameter counts or structure.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 System Card
sources.evidence: The full extracted later card was checked for exact GPT-5.5 Instant names and numerical/structural disclosures. No exact Instant entry or count was found; GPT-5.5 Thinking and successor specifications are not transferred.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra System Card
sources.evidence: The full extracted later card was checked for exact GPT-5.5 Instant references. No exact Instant entry or production count/architecture disclosure was found; successor model evidence is not substituted.

sources.title: Public Summary of Training Content for GPT-5.5
sources.evidence: The July 29 training summary names GPT-5.5 without identifying Instant. Its data quantities and modalities are training-content disclosures, not parameter counts or API modalities; it cannot independently establish exact Instant properties.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Vision-capable models receive PDF extracted text and page images through Responses; Chat Completions also accepts PDF files. Combined with exact Instant vision and historically documented API availability, PDF is an input format, not a separate native modality.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: The current page has no exact gpt-5.5-instant or chat-latest shutdown notice. Older gpt-5.2-chat-latest and gpt-5.3-chat-latest notices do not apply; absence of a notice does not prove which model currently serves a mutable alias.

sources.title: Model Release Notes
sources.evidence: May 28 explicitly updates GPT-5.5 Instant in ChatGPT and API. October 14 retires GPT-5.5 from product surfaces and says API access is unaffected, but does not separately identify Instant; no exact Instant shutdown is inferred from that broad notice.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Sections 2.2 and 9.1 grant limited nonexclusive service/API access and reserve service IP. Supports a descriptive Proprietary hosted-service classification, not a downloadable-weight license.

sources.title: OpenAI model inventory
sources.evidence: The current official catalog lists chat-latest and separately lists gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b as open-weight models. No downloadable GPT-5.5 Instant weights are offered in checked primary release/catalog material.

sources.title: Attempted GPT-5.5 Instant API model documentation
sources.evidence: Direct request returned HTTP 404. The catalog identifier is not thereby verified as a standalone OpenAI API model ID.

sources.title: Models.dev GPT-5.5 Instant record
sources.evidence: The original lead was inspected. It derives 400K capacity from chat-latest and asserts a compact model description; both require exact-model primary verification.

name.note: Official model name. The catalog identity is retained; documented launch API access used chat-latest, not a verified standalone gpt-5.5-instant endpoint.

developer.note: Developer identified in its own release and system card.

family.note: Normalize the explicitly named generation; this does not assert shared weights with GPT-5.5 Thinking or Pro.

release_date.note: Explicit public release in ChatGPT and the API. The May 4 card cover is a document date; later alias updates are not the original model launch.

open_weights.note: Checked official release and inventory distribute the model through hosted services and provide no downloadable Instant weights.

license.note: Descriptive hosted-service access classification; not an SPDX or open-weight license.

parameters_b.note: No total production count is disclosed in the original exact-model card or later health/engineering materials. Later cards and targeted first-party training/interpretability/count searches found no exact Instant numerical disclosure. Training tokens and benchmark scores are not parameters.

active_parameters_b.note: No per-token active count or activation topology was disclosed in the checked exact-model materials and later-card searches. Do not equate total and active counts or infer dense/MoE layout.

architecture.note: Qualified cross-source inference: an exact GPT-5.5 Instant delegation example is followed in the same engineering section by explicit frontier-model prompt caching, and the pre-GPT-5.6 guide explains Transformer KV projections. This example-bound operational classification does not establish complete block composition, dense/MoE layout or counts. The voice model KV passage is excluded.

context_window.note: Clear 400K: the current mutable chat-latest page no longer binds its 400K limit to this exact model. Historical Azure May/June versions list 128K, but those provider limits do not prove the OpenAI-hosted maximum. No sufficiently scoped primary OpenAI capacity was found.

modalities.note: Native text/image input and text output are supported by the exact release/card. PDF is retained as an API document format converted into text and page images, using the documented launch alias, vision and Chat Completions/Responses support. GPT-Live integration does not make audio a native Instant modality.

reasoning.note: The exact original card says deployed at low reasoning effort and tested at xhigh; Azure documents fixed nonzero effort. This verifies internal reasoning, not exposed selectable effort controls, full Thinking behavior, or the unrelated May 7 older-Instant training incident.

tool_call.note: Exact launch describes web search; the provider version table explicitly documents functions/tools, and later engineering describes Instant delegation with tool round trips. No current mutable-alias-only feature is transferred.

description.value: OpenAI conversational model with image understanding, internal reasoning and tool use; launched in the API through chat-latest.
description.note: Replace unsupported compact-size and high-volume marketing claims with documented capabilities and the API identity boundary.

patch.notes: Released May 5, 2026 through ChatGPT and the mutable chat-latest API alias; the original card cover is May 4. The catalog ID is not verified as a standalone API endpoint. Subsequent alias updates include May 28, June 24, August 6 and October 7. Current chat-latest documentation states 400K, while Azure May/June versions state 128K; neither establishes an exact OpenAI-hosted capacity for the original model, so context is unverified. Reasoning was deployed at low effort; xhigh was used for capability evaluation, not documented as a selectable public control. PDF is an API format. Transformer is a qualified inference from example-bound Instant delegation caching and the pre-GPT-5.6 KV guide, not a complete topology disclosure. Total/active parameters remain undisclosed. No exact API shutdown notice was found, and current alias identity or endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Confirm May 5 release, exact Instant identity, proprietary hosted distribution, internal low-effort reasoning and tool use. Normalize GPT-5.5 family; add qualified broad Transformer inference from later deployment engineering; replace unsupported compact-model description. Clear 400K context because current mutable-alias limits lack exact historical binding and Azure version limits differ. Counts remain undisclosed after original/later exact-model and successor-card checks.
